content.text: for testing, see:
http://fedora-commons.org/confluence/display/DEV/FeSL+Installation

Basically for sanity testing: install dbxml, set env variables. Install Fedora with FeSL enabled (may as well set APIA auth=true for testing). Add some non-admin users to fedora-users.xml. Run admin client and test ingest/purge. Try FieldSearch (/fedora/search) as fedoraAdmin (succeed) and non admin user (denied).
Having some trouble installing (via installer) on Windows:
fedora.utilities.install.OptionDefinition wants to find db.jar and dbxml.jar under $DBXML_HOME/lib
Installing Oracle/Berkeley DBXml from binaries on Windows leaves these jars under $DBXML_HOME/jar
Trying to specify the path above leaves the installer trying to find the jars in $DBXML_HOME/jar/lib, which doesn't exist.
DBXml v. 2.5.13, Windows vista (64 bit)
Ben, thanks for turning that up. Just the sort of thing a Windows sanity test was supposed to turn up. Checked in a fix if you don't mind giving it another go. Thanks!
TestRESTAPI.patch
Fixes test failure on testIngest method of TestRESTAPI.
Test was looking for Location header at a specific index in the headers array. Changed this to obtain the header by name instead.
This fix also resolves the testFailure on the testChunked method as the testIngest is a dependency.
Eddie-

Sorry for the lag in response.  The install went off without a hitch with the release code. I unfortunately have to build dbxml from source for it to actually run on my Windows development box (64 bit binaries not available!), so my follow-up will be delayed a bit.

Closing this issue as it was nominally delivered and closed for the 3.3 release despite some outstanding failures in the configC specific unit tests. Will open new issues to tracking remaining configC test failures
This work is still coming together, but with include major improvements for Fedora's AuthN and AuthZ components.
Futher details can be found here:
http://fedora-commons.org/confluence/x/h4Ov

FESL should eventually replace the default AuthN/AuthZ functionality built in to Fedora.  If there's a need for people to migrate policies, there should be a period of overlap (where the "old way" and "new way" work)...hopefully this can be the case for Fedora 3.3
